lucas (acme): Hey — we're seeing very high latency (200-400ms) and a bunch of requests hitting us-west even though our client sets region=eu-west. Request id: r-9f4a2b. Any idea?
anna (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact header your client is sending and a curl repro?
lucas (acme): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_***" -H "x-client-region: \"eu-west\"" -d '{"model":"small","prompt":"hi"}' 
anna (support): Thanks. Noted the extra quotes around eu-west. Can you confirm your SDK version?
lucas (acme): Using our in-house wrapper over the JS SDK. We pass region from user config, haven't seen quotes before. SDK is 2.3.1.
router-bot: routing-check r-9f4a2b -> selected_edge: us-west-1 (fallback), reason: unrecognized region token '\"eu-west\"' (parser: header-parse-v1)
anna (support): @devon can you take a look? Looks like router treated the header value as literal including quotes so it wasn't matched to eu-west. Customer insists they set eu-west.
devon (eng): On it — quick q: do you have packet capture / raw request headers from their proxy? I want to see if the quotes are added by the client or mutated in transit. Also what is the exact header name (x-client-region vs x-region)?
lucas (acme): It's x-client-region. We just logged the outbound header from our app and it shows: x-client-region: "eu-west" (weird). We think a serialization layer may be escaping it.
sasha (oncall): Noted. I'll keep an eye on router metrics for fallback count spikes.
devon (eng): Reproduced locally by sending quotes — router parser uses simple token match expecting /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, so a value with quotes fails validation and falls back to default region. Short term: we can loosen parser to trim surrounding quotes/whitespace and accept. Long term: normalize header values across SDKs.
anna (support): What's the customer impact? latency, wrong billing region?
devon (eng): Impact: cross-region latency and regional billing mismatch if they rely on eu pricing. The router fallback is intentional for safety.
lucas (acme): Can you disable fallback for our org while we patch client? We want errors instead of silent reroute.
devon (eng): We can't disable fallback universally but we can add a per-tenant strict-parsing flag. I'll open an internal change request. For immediate workaround: 1) Advise customer to strip quotes in their wrapper. 2) We will deploy a patch to router to trim surrounding quotes for header parsing (hotfix). 3) Patch JS SDK to normalize region before sending.
anna (support): Action items: - lucas: strip quotes in your wrapper or upgrade once we release SDK patch (ETA below). - devon: hotfix router to trim quotes + add metric for malformed-region-header. - sasha: monitor fallback metric and alert if >0.5% per min.
devon (eng): Hotfix plan: patch router parser to run region = region.trim().replace(/^\"|\"$/g, '') then re-evaluate routing. Deploy to canary in us-east in 30m, roll to control plane in 2 hours if no regressions. I'll add a rollout note.
devon (eng): SDK fix: add normalizeRegion() helper that lowercases, trims whitespace/quotes, maps aliases (eu, eu-west -> eu-west). PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference-js/pulls/492. Will cut 2.3.2 once CI passes.
lucas (acme): Thanks. Any temporary header rewrite we can do at our CDN edge? Our CDN supports header transforms but we wanted to avoid that. Might do it for now.
anna (support): If you do CDN rewrite set x-client-region to eu-west (no quotes). Good temporary measure.
sasha (oncall): Alert rule added: metric router.malformed_region_headers increased from 0.003% to 0.8% in last 5m for org acme — investigating.
devon (eng): Root cause summary: some client wrapper serializes header values with JSON quoting, e.g., setting header value to JSON.stringify(region). Router's strict parser treated the value as invalid and used default fallback region. Remediation: normalize header values in router and push SDK change.
anna (support): Timeline: hotfix to router canary in 30m -> full rollout 2h. SDK PR authoring now, release in ~4h pending tests. Customer guidance: CDN rewrite or quick fix in wrapper.
lucas (acme): Appreciate the quick response. We'll enable CDN header rewrite and roll our fix. Please keep me posted when SDK cut is done.
devon (eng): Will update this thread when canary looks good and when PR merges.
anna (support): Marking as escalated -> eng. Tracking internal ticket INF-4621. I'll follow up with billing if any charge region corrections are needed.
lucas (acme): One last ask — can you retroactively tag the affected request ids with 'misrouted' so we can reconcile logs? Request id r-9f4a2b and others.
sasha (oncall): I'll add labels to trace r-9f4a2b and run a reconciliation job for last 24h for org acme.
devon (eng): Canary deployed, router parser trim/strip running on canary edge. No errors in 10m smoke test. Rolling to control plane in 90m. SDK PR merged to main, CI green. Cutting 2.3.2 now.
anna (support): SDK 2.3.2 published. Release notes: "normalize region header values (trim, unquote, lowercase)". Closing loop with customer once they confirm. :thumbsup:
lucas (acme): Confirmed after CDN rewrite and upgrading to 2.3.2 latency back to normal and requests hit eu-west. Thanks everyone! :tada:
